credits.note: The rosette at the centre (inner circle from one chord, star lines joining its points 150° apart) follows her construction.

credits.source: Drawing of the Bou Inania pattern

given.A: Any point to the right of O. OA is the radius of the first circle.

steps.text: Rule a horizontal line through O and A and draw the first circle about O through A. Keep this opening.

Put the compass point where the circle meets the line on the right, and draw a circle through O; do the same on the left. Rule the vertical through O, and draw the same circle about its top and bottom points.

The four circles cut the first one at eight more points: it is divided into twelve. Rule the lines through O and opposite points, then halve every angle between them, so there is a line through O every 15°.
Halve the angles between the lines at 0° and 15°, and at 15° and 30°: two more lines through O, at 7.5° and 22.5°.
Mark where the 75° line cuts the circle and join that point to the point on the left of the horizontal. Where this chord crosses the vertical, draw a circle about O: Samira Mian’s inner circle.
Mark where the inner circle meets the lines at 0°, 30°, 60° and so on, and join each of these points to the one 150° round. The twelve lines make the twelve-pointed star (set A).

Draw circles of the first size about the points at 0° and 30°. They cross outside the first circle on the 15° line: the bigger circle about O passes through that crossing. Through it, rule the line at right angles to the horizontal, and turn it round: the big twelve-sided figure (set E).

Where a star line crosses a side of the big figure, rule a line at right angles to the 7.5° line, and its mirror image in the horizontal; turn both round. These 24 lines make the small five-pointed stars. Through the point of the first circle at 30°, rule the line at right angles to the 30° line: it just touches the circle. Turn it round (helper lines). Where the lines touching the circle at 30° and −30° cross the horizontal, rule a line at right angles to it; turn it round. These lines close the brown pentagons.

Where a side of the big figure crosses one of the 24 lines, rule a line at right angles to the 22.5° line; turn it round in eighths: the octagon of the corner stars. Where an octagon side crosses one of the 24 lines, rule a line at right angles to the horizontal; turn it round in quarters: the frame, and the edge of the tile.

Where a star line crosses one of the pentagon lines, rule a line at right angles to the horizontal, and turn it round: the inner side of the ring round the shields. Where two of the 24 lines cross on the horizontal, rule a line at right angles to the 15° line; turn it round: the points of the ring round the shields.

Where a side of the big figure crosses one of the last-but-one set, rule a line at right angles to the horizontal; turn it round. These carry the star lines on into the corners. Where the frame crosses a pentagon line, rule a line at right angles to the 45° line; turn it round in quarters: the lines across the corners. Where a side of the big figure crosses a pentagon line, rule a line at right angles to the 15° line; turn it round. Where two of the 24 lines cross on the 45° line, rule a line at right angles to the 15° line; turn it round.

Mark the corners of the pattern: every point where the pattern turns or ends. Where the inner band on the right (or top) side breaks, rule a line across to the left (or bottom) side: the band breaks there too, because the next tile lies over it.

The tile: the square between the big figure’s right and top sides and the frame’s left and bottom sides. Its copies overlap by one band, so the two lines along each side of the tile fall on the two lines of the next tile.

ink.text: Ink the twelve-pointed star and its petals, the ring of small stars and pentagons, the ring round the shields, and the bands and corner stars out to the frame.

pattern.text: Repeat the square edge to edge: neighbouring tiles share the frame band, and the corner pieces of four tiles meet in an eight-pointed star.
